- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java 11 in-memory spreadsheet processing contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java, src/main/java/Cell.java, src/main/java/Row.java, src/main/java/Sorters.java, src/main/java/Sheet.java, src/main/java/Workbook.java, src/main/java/ValueParser.java, src/main/java/Filters.java, src/main/java/Aggregations.java, src/main/java/CsvIO.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; all project classes are in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Surefire plugin. Java streams are forbidden throughout this small repository, especially `Stream.toList()` which does not exist in Java 11; use ordinary bounded loops and `java.util.ArrayList`
- ProcessingReport starts rowsRead, rowsKept, and rowsWritten at zero and owns a LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts. incrementRowsRead/incrementRowsKept/incrementRowsWritten add exactly one; recordInvalid(column) adds exactly one for that key; getters return counters; invalidCounts returns an unmodifiable defensive LinkedHashMap copy. No method changes an unrelated counter
- Cell is immutable: Cell.of(String raw) maps null to the empty string and otherwise preserves the string; raw() returns it and isBlank() tests raw.trim().isEmpty(). Row copies its header and cells, get(String column) returns the cell at the first equal header or Cell.of("") if absent, and header(), cells(), and asStringMap() return unmodifiable defensive values
- Sorters.Order(String column,boolean ascending) exposes column() and ascending(). Sorters.comparator(List<Order>) compares Cell.raw() strings in order, puts blank values last regardless of direction, and is deterministic. Sheet copies name/header/rows, exposes name(), header(), rows(), filter(Predicate<Row>,ProcessingReport), and sort(List<Sorters.Order>); filter increments rowsKept exactly once per retained row and neither operation changes rowsRead or rowsWritten
- Workbook is only an in-memory named-sheet container with addSheet, getSheet returning Optional, and sheetNames returning an unmodifiable defensive set
- ValueParser.toDouble(String raw,String column,ProcessingReport report) trims input, returns null without recording for null/blank, returns Double.valueOf for valid input, and on invalid input calls report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once then returns null. Filters.equals and contains perform string predicates; numericGreaterThan uses ValueParser once per tested row
- Aggregations exposes count, sum, average, min, and max. Each numeric method visits every row once and calls ValueParser.toDouble exactly once for that row; blank and invalid values are ignored, sum/average return 0.0 when no numeric value, min/max return null. Therefore one invocation of sum over one invalid `bad` cell records exactly one invalid count; tests must use a fresh ProcessingReport for each independent aggregation instead of expecting several aggregation calls to record one combined invalid event
- CsvIO has exactly two public static operations: `Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report)` and `String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report)`. The format is deliberately simple comma-separated text with no quoted commas. Import treats the first line as header, preserves empty fields by using split with a negative limit, pads short data rows, ignores excess cells, and calls incrementRowsRead exactly once per data row. Export emits the header and every data row with commas and newline separators, calls incrementRowsWritten exactly once per data row, and never changes rowsRead/rowsKept. There is no report-free export overload and no Reader/Writer/filesystem API
- Main.main uses one fixed in-memory CSV string, fresh reports for logically separate operations, prints at most one concise deterministic summary, and returns normally without input, network, filesystem, GUI, threads, clock, or randomness
- Because all project classes are in the unnamed/default package, MainTest imports only org.junit.jupiter.api.Test, static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions members, and ordinary java.util classes; it directly refers to project classes by simple name and must never emit invalid lines such as `import Sheet;`, `import CsvIO;`, or `import ProcessingReport;`
- MainTest contains exactly three concise tests and uses no streams: (1) runtime invokes `Main.main(new String[0])` and returns normally; (2) pipeline uses the literal CSV `Name,Country,Sales
Alice,US,1000
Bob,CA,1500
Charlie,US,2000`, imports with reportImport and asserts rowsRead==3, filters Country US with reportFilter and asserts rowsKept==2, then MUST literally assert `assertEquals("Alice", filteredRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Charlie", filteredRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`, sorts those two rows descending by Name and MUST literally assert `assertEquals("Charlie", sortedRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Alice", sortedRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`, then sums Sales with a fresh reportAggregation and asserts 3000.0 and empty invalidCounts; Row itself has no raw() method, so `filteredRows.get(1).raw()` and every equivalent direct Row.raw() call are forbidden; (3) invalid/round-trip uses literal CSV `Name,Sales
Alice,1000
Bob,bad
Charlie,
Dana,2000`, calls sum exactly once with a fresh reportAggregation and asserts 3000.0 plus invalidCounts().get("Sales")==1, exports with a fresh reportExport and asserts rowsWritten==4, re-imports with a fresh reportReimport and asserts rowsRead==4, identical header, four rows, and Bob's Sales remains `bad`
- no test expects rowsKept immediately after import, no test expects rowsWritten after import or before calling the report-taking toCsvString, and no test reuses one ProcessingReport across sum/average/min/max while expecting only one invalid count

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java 11 in-memory spreadsheet processing contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java, src/main/java/Cell.java, src/main/java/Row.java, src/main/java/Sorters.java, src/main/java/Sheet.java, src/main/java/Workbook.java, src/main/java/ValueParser.java, src/main/java/Filters.java, src/main/java/Aggregations.java, src/main/java/CsvIO.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; all project classes are in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Surefire plugin. Java streams are forbidden throughout this small repository, especially `Stream.toList()` which does not exist in Java 11; use ordinary bounded loops and `java.util.ArrayList`
- ProcessingReport starts rowsRead, rowsKept, and rowsWritten at zero and owns a LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts. incrementRowsRead/incrementRowsKept/incrementRowsWritten add exactly one; recordInvalid(column) adds exactly one for that key; getters return counters; invalidCounts returns an unmodifiable defensive LinkedHashMap copy. No method changes an unrelated counter
- Cell is immutable: Cell.of(String raw) maps null to the empty string and otherwise preserves the string; raw() returns it and isBlank() tests raw.trim().isEmpty(). Row copies its header and cells, get(String column) returns the cell at the first equal header or Cell.of("") if absent, and header(), cells(), and asStringMap() return unmodifiable defensive values
- Sorters.Order(String column,boolean ascending) exposes column() and ascending(). Sorters.comparator(List<Order>) compares Cell.raw() strings in order, puts blank values last regardless of direction, and is deterministic. Sheet copies name/header/rows, exposes name(), header(), rows(), filter(Predicate<Row>,ProcessingReport), and sort(List<Sorters.Order>); filter increments rowsKept exactly once per retained row and neither operation changes rowsRead or rowsWritten
- Workbook is only an in-memory named-sheet container with addSheet, getSheet returning Optional, and sheetNames returning an unmodifiable defensive set
- ValueParser.toDouble(String raw,String column,ProcessingReport report) trims input, returns null without recording for null/blank, returns Double.valueOf for valid input, and on invalid input calls report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once then returns null. Filters.equals and contains perform string predicates; numericGreaterThan uses ValueParser once per tested row
- Aggregations exposes count, sum, average, min, and max. Each numeric method visits every row once and calls ValueParser.toDouble exactly once for that row; blank and invalid values are ignored, sum/average return 0.0 when no numeric value, min/max return null. Therefore one invocation of sum over one invalid `bad` cell records exactly one invalid count; tests must use a fresh ProcessingReport for each independent aggregation instead of expecting several aggregation calls to record one combined invalid event
- CsvIO has exactly two public static operations: `Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report)` and `String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report)`. The format is deliberately simple comma-separated text with no quoted commas. Import treats the first line as header, preserves empty fields by using split with a negative limit, pads short data rows, ignores excess cells, and calls incrementRowsRead exactly once per data row.   - public static final class Order
    - private final String column; private final boolean ascending.
    - public Order(String column, boolean ascending)
    - public String column(): returns column.
    - public boolean ascending(): returns ascending.
  - public static Comparator<Row> comparator(List<Order> orders): returns a comparator that for each Order compares the corresponding Cell.raw() strings; blanks (cell.isBlank()) always sort after non-blanks regardless of ascending/descending; for non-blank comparisons use String.compareTo; apply ascending flag by reversing sign if needed; if tie across all orders, deterministically tie-break by comparing full Row as concatenated raw strings (e.g., iterate header order) to avoid nondeterminism; never use Java streams.

src/main/java/Sheet.java:
- public final class Sheet
  - private final String name; private final List<String> header; private final List<Row> rows.
  - public Sheet(String name, List<String> header, List<Row> rows): copies inputs defensively.
  - public String name(): returns name.
  - public List<String> header(): unmodifiable defensive header view.
  - public List<Row> rows(): unmodifiable defensive rows view.
  - public Sheet filter(Predicate<Row> predicate, ProcessingReport report): builds a new Sheet with only rows where predicate.test(row) is true; for each retained row, call report.incrementRowsKept() exactly once; does not change report.rowsRead or rowsWritten; header/name preserved.
  - public Sheet sort(List<Sorters.Order> orders): returns a new Sheet with rows sorted by Sorters.comparator(orders); no counter changes.

src/main/java/Workbook.java:
- public final class Workbook
  - private final LinkedHashMap<String, Sheet> sheets = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  - public Workbook()
  - public void addSheet(Sheet sheet): inserts/overwrites by sheet.name().
  - public Optional<Sheet> getSheet(String name): returns Optional.of(sheet) if present, else Optional.empty().
  - public Set<String> sheetNames(): returns unmodifiable defensive set copy preserving insertion order if applicable.

src/main/java/ValueParser.java:
- public final class ValueParser
  - public static Double toDouble(String raw, String column, ProcessingReport report): if raw==null or raw.trim().isEmpty(), return null without recording; else attempt Double.valueOf(trimmed); on NumberFormatException, call report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once and return null.

src/main/java/Filters.java:
- public final class Filters
  - public static Predicate<Row> equals(String column, String value): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().equals(value).
  - public static Predicate<Row> contains(String column, String fragment): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().contains(fragment).
  - public static Predicate<Row> numericGreaterThan(String column, double threshold, ProcessingReport report): for a given row, call ValueParser.toDouble once with row.get(column).raw(); if null return false; else return parsed > threshold.

src/main/java/Aggregations.java:
- public final class Aggregations
  - public static int count(Sheet sheet): returns sheet.rows().size().
  - public static double sum(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate rows once, call ValueParser.toDouble once per row; accumulate non-null values; ignore blanks/invalids; return 0.0 if none.
  - public static double average(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): as sum but divide by count of numeric values; return 0.0 if no numeric values.
  - public static Double min(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track smallest non-null; return null if none.
  - public static Double max(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track largest non-null; return null if none.
  - All methods must not use Java streams; use for loops and ArrayList.

src/main/java/CsvIO.java:
- public final class CsvIO
  - public static Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report): split by '\n' retaining order; first line is header split by ',' with negative limit to preserve trailing empties; for each subsequent line (data row), split with negative limit; pad to header length with empty strings; ignore excess cells; construct Cell for each field; wrap in Row; increment report.incrementRowsRead() exactly once per data row; return new Sheet(name, header, dataRows).
  - public static String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report): build string with header line (comma-joined) followed by each row as comma-joined cell.raw(); for every data row written, call report.incrementRowsWritten() exactly once; must not modify rowsRead or rowsKept; use '\n' line separators; do not quote commas or escape.

src/main/java/Main.java:
- public final class Main
  - public static void main(String[] args): prepare a fixed in-memory CSV string; use fresh ProcessingReport for each phase (import, filter, aggregation, export); invoke CsvIO.importCsvFromString, Sheet.filter, Sheet.sort, Aggregations.sum, CsvIO.toCsvString; print one concise deterministic summary; no input, no filesystem/network, no randomness, no threads, no streams.

- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Surefire plugin. Java streams are forbidden throughout this small repository, especially `Stream.toList()` which does not exist in Java 11; use ordinary bounded loops and `java.util.ArrayList`
- ProcessingReport starts rowsRead, rowsKept, and rowsWritten at zero and owns a LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts. incrementRowsRead/incrementRowsKept/incrementRowsWritten add exactly one; recordInvalid(column) adds exactly one for that key; getters return counters; invalidCounts returns an unmodifiable defensive LinkedHashMap copy. No method changes an unrelated counter
- Cell is immutable: Cell.of(String raw) maps null to the empty string and otherwise preserves the string; raw() returns it and isBlank() tests raw.trim().isEmpty(). Row copies its header and cells, get(String column) returns the cell at the first equal header or Cell.of("") if absent, and header(), cells(), and asStringMap() return unmodifiable defensive values
- Sorters.Order(String column,boolean ascending) exposes column() and ascending(). Sorters.comparator(List<Order>) compares Cell.raw() strings in order, puts blank values last regardless of direction, and is deterministic. Sheet copies name/header/rows, exposes name(), header(), rows(), filter(Predicate<Row>,ProcessingReport), and sort(List<Sorters.Order>); filter increments rowsKept exactly once per retained row and neither operation changes rowsRead or rowsWritten
- Workbook is only an in-memory named-sheet container with addSheet, getSheet returning Optional, and sheetNames returning an unmodifiable defensive set
- ValueParser.toDouble(String raw,String column,ProcessingReport report) trims input, returns null without recording for null/blank, returns Double.valueOf for valid input, and on invalid input calls report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once then returns null. Filters.equals and contains perform string predicates; numericGreaterThan uses ValueParser once per tested row
- Aggregations exposes count, sum, average, min, and max. Each numeric method visits every row once and calls ValueParser.toDouble exactly once for that row; blank and invalid values are ignored, sum/average return 0.0 when no numeric value, min/max return null. Therefore one invocation of sum over one invalid `bad` cell records exactly one invalid count; tests must use a fresh ProcessingReport for each independent aggregation instead of expecting several aggregation calls to record one combined invalid event
- CsvIO has exactly two public static operations: `Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report)` and `String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report)`. The format is deliberately simple comma-separated text with no quoted commas. Import treats the first line as header, preserves empty fields by using split with a negative limit, pads short data rows, ignores excess cells, and calls incrementRowsRead exactly once per data row. Export emits the header and every data row with commas and newline separators, calls incrementRowsWritten exactly once per data row, and never changes rowsRead/rowsKept. There is no report-free export overload and no Reader/Writer/filesystem API

Bob,CA,1500
Charlie,US,2000`, imports with reportImport and asserts rowsRead==3, filters Country US with reportFilter and asserts rowsKept==2, then MUST literally assert `assertEquals("Alice", filteredRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Charlie", filteredRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`, sorts those two rows descending by Name and MUST literally assert `assertEquals("Charlie", sortedRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Alice", sortedRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`, then sums Sales with a fresh reportAggregation and asserts 3000.0 and empty invalidCounts; Row itself has no raw() method, so `filteredRows.get(1).raw()` and every equivalent direct Row.raw() call are forbidden; (3) invalid/round-trip uses literal CSV `Name,Sales
Alice,1000
Bob,bad
Charlie,
Dana,2000`, calls sum exactly once with a fresh reportAggregation and asserts 3000.0 plus invalidCounts().get("Sales")==1, exports with a fresh reportExport and asserts rowsWritten==4, re-imports with a fresh reportReimport and asserts rowsRead==4, identical header, four rows, and Bob's Sales remains `bad`
- no test expects rowsKept immediately after import, no test expects rowsWritten after import or before calling the report-taking toCsvString, and no test reuses one ProcessingReport across sum/average/min/max while expecting only one invalid count

src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java:
- public final class ProcessingReport
  - private int rowsRead, rowsKept, rowsWritten initialized to 0.
  - private LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts initialized empty.
  - public ProcessingReport()
  - public void incrementRowsRead(): increments rowsRead by exactly 1.
  - public void incrementRowsKept(): increments rowsKept by exactly 1.
  - public void incrementRowsWritten(): increments rowsWritten by exactly 1.
  - public void recordInvalid(String column): adds 1 to invalidCounts for key column exactly once per call; must not increment other counters.
  - public int getRowsRead(), getRowsKept(), getRowsWritten(): return respective counters.
  - public LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts(): returns an unmodifiable defensive copy preserving insertion order. No method changes unrelated counters.

src/main/java/Cell.java:
- public final class Cell
  - private final String raw.
  - public static Cell of(String raw): if raw==null, store empty string; else store raw as-is.
  - public String raw(): returns stored raw.
  - public boolean isBlank(): returns raw.trim().isEmpty(). Immutable; no setters.

src/main/java/Row.java:
- public final class Row
  - private final List<String> header; private final List<Cell> cells; both copied defensively in constructor.
  - public Row(List<String> header, List<Cell> cells): copies inputs and may pad internal cells to header size using Cell.of("") if needed.
  - public List<String> header(): returns unmodifiable defensive copy or unmodifiable view that cannot be mutated by caller.
  - public List<Cell> cells(): returns unmodifiable defensive view of cells list.
  - public Cell get(String column): finds first index i in header with header.get(i).equals(column); if found and i < cells.size(), return cells.get(i); if not found or i>=cells.size(), return Cell.of("").
  - public LinkedHashMap<String,String> asStringMap(): builds an ordered map of header->cells[i].raw() for each header index; if cells shorter, empty string for missing.

src/main/java/Sorters.java:
- public final class Sorters
  - public static final class Order
    - private final String column; private final boolean ascending.
    - public Order(String column, boolean ascending)
    - public String column(): returns column.
    - public boolean ascending(): returns ascending.
  - public static Comparator<Row> comparator(List<Order> orders): returns a comparator that for each Order compares the corresponding Cell.raw() strings; blanks (cell.isBlank()) always sort after non-blanks regardless of ascending/descending; for non-blank comparisons use String.compareTo; apply ascending flag by reversing sign if needed; if tie across all orders, deterministically tie-break by comparing full Row as concatenated raw strings (e.g., iterate header order) to avoid nondeterminism; never use Java streams.

src/main/java/Sheet.java:
- public final class Sheet
  - private final String name; private final List<String> header; private final List<Row> rows.
  - public Sheet(String name, List<String> header, List<Row> rows): copies inputs defensively.
  - public String name(): returns name.
  - public List<String> header(): unmodifiable defensive header view.
  - public List<Row> rows(): unmodifiable defensive rows view.
  - public Sheet filter(Predicate<Row> predicate, ProcessingReport report): builds a new Sheet with only rows where predicate.test(row) is true; for each retained row, call report.incrementRowsKept() exactly once; does not change report.rowsRead or rowsWritten; header/name preserved.
  - public Sheet sort(List<Sorters.Order> orders): returns a new Sheet with rows sorted by Sorters.comparator(orders); no counter changes.

src/main/java/Workbook.java:
- public final class Workbook
  - private final LinkedHashMap<String, Sheet> sheets = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  - public Workbook()
  - public void addSheet(Sheet sheet): inserts/overwrites by sheet.name().
  - public Optional<Sheet> getSheet(String name): returns Optional.of(sheet) if present, else Optional.empty().
  - public Set<String> sheetNames(): returns unmodifiable defensive set copy preserving insertion order if applicable.

src/main/java/ValueParser.java:
- public final class ValueParser
  - public static Double toDouble(String raw, String column, ProcessingReport report): if raw==null or raw.trim().isEmpty(), return null without recording; else attempt Double.valueOf(trimmed); on NumberFormatException, call report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once and return null.

src/main/java/Filters.java:
- public final class Filters
  - public static Predicate<Row> equals(String column, String value): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().equals(value).
  - public static Predicate<Row> contains(String column, String fragment): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().contains(fragment).
  - public static Predicate<Row> numericGreaterThan(String column, double threshold, ProcessingReport report): for a given row, call ValueParser.toDouble once with row.get(column).raw(); if null return false; else return parsed > threshold.

src/main/java/Aggregations.java:
- public final class Aggregations
  - public static int count(Sheet sheet): returns sheet.rows().size().
  - public static double sum(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate rows once, call ValueParser.toDouble once per row; accumulate non-null values; ignore blanks/invalids; return 0.0 if none.
  - public static double average(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): as sum but divide by count of numeric values; return 0.0 if no numeric values.
  - public static Double min(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track smallest non-null; return null if none.
  - public static Double max(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track largest non-null; return null if none.
  - All methods must not use Java streams; use for loops and ArrayList.

src/main/java/CsvIO.java:
- public final class CsvIO
  - public static Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report): split by '\n' retaining order; first line is header split by ',' with negative limit to preserve trailing empties; for each subsequent line (data row), split with negative limit; pad to header length with empty strings; ignore excess cells; construct Cell for each field; wrap in Row; increment report.incrementRowsRead() exactly once per data row; return new Sheet(name, header, dataRows).
  - public static String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report): build string with header line (comma-joined) followed by each row as comma-joined cell.raw(); for every data row written, call report.incrementRowsWritten() exactly once; must not modify rowsRead or rowsKept; use '\n' line separators; do not quote commas or escape.

src/main/java/Main.java:
- public final class Main
  - public static void main(String[] args): prepare a fixed in-memory CSV string; use fresh ProcessingReport for each phase (import, filter, aggregation, export); invoke CsvIO.importCsvFromString, Sheet.filter, Sheet.sort, Aggregations.sum, CsvIO.toCsvString; print one concise deterministic summary; no input, no filesystem/network, no randomness, no threads, no streams.

src/test/java/MainTest.java:
- JUnit 5 tests only; default package; imports only org.junit.jupiter.api.Test and static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.* plus java.util.*; refer to project classes by simple names; no explicit project imports.
- Exactly three tests:
  1) runtime invokes Main.main(new String[0]) returns normally.
  2) three-row pipeline uses literal CSV `Name,Country,Sales\nAlice,US,1000\nBob,CA,1500\nCharlie,US,2000`; import with fresh reportImport assert rowsRead==3; filter Country=="US" with fresh reportFilter assert rowsKept==2; literally assert `assertEquals("Alice", filteredRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Charlie", filteredRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`; sort those rows descending by Name and literally assert `assertEquals("Charlie", sortedRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Alice", sortedRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`; sum Sales with fresh reportAggregation assert 3000.0 and invalidCounts empty.
  3) invalid/round-trip uses literal CSV `Name,Sales\nAlice,1000\nBob,bad\nCharlie,\nDana,2000`; call sum exactly once with fresh reportAggregation assert 3000.0 and invalidCounts().get("Sales")==1; export with fresh reportExport assert rowsWritten==4; re-import with fresh reportReimport assert rowsRead==4, identical header, four rows, and Bob's Sales remains `bad`.

Global constraints:
- All classes in default (unnamed) package; tests must not import project classes.
- Java streams are forbidden across all files; use loops and ArrayList.
- CsvIO exposes exactly two public static methods as specified; no overloads.
- Each independent operation uses a fresh ProcessingReport; counters have precise ownership semantics.
- Allowed dependency direction: ProcessingReport, Cell -> Row -> Sorters/Sheet -> Workbook/Filters/Aggregations/CsvIO -> Main -> MainTest. Tests call public APIs only.","Shared Knowledge":"This repository is a headless Java 11 Maven project implementing in-memory Excel-like data processing with CSV import/export, filtering, sorting, and aggregations. All implementation classes live in the default package under src/main/java and are dependency-ordered. ProcessingReport owns counters and invalid counts; Cell and Row are immutable-like with defensive copies; Sorters provides multi-column comparator with blanks-last; Sheet performs filter and sort without mutating counters except rowsKept during filter; Workbook is an in-memory container; ValueParser provides numeric parsing with exact invalid recording semantics; Filters and Aggregations are pure rules calling ValueParser exactly once per visited row; CsvIO implements two static methods for CSV import/export with precise counter effects; Main demonstrates a fixed pipeline with fresh reports per phase; MainTest (JUnit 5) contains exactly three tests, imports only JUnit and java.util, references project classes by simple names in the unnamed package, and never uses Java streams.","Execution Protocol":"Build and test with: mvn -q test. Runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java (default package). Single protocol-level test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java with exactly three tests. Tests are deterministic, headless, offline, and non-interactive. No additional test files are present. No network, filesystem, clock, GUI, threads, or randomness are used.","Anything UNCLEAR":""}

src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java:
- public final class ProcessingReport
  - private int rowsRead, rowsKept, rowsWritten initialized to 0.
  - private LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts initialized empty.
  - public ProcessingReport()
  - public void incrementRowsRead(): increments rowsRead by exactly 1.
  - public void incrementRowsKept(): increments rowsKept by exactly 1.
  - public void incrementRowsWritten(): increments rowsWritten by exactly 1.
  - public void recordInvalid(String column): adds 1 to invalidCounts for key column exactly once per call; must not increment other counters.
  - public int getRowsRead(), getRowsKept(), getRowsWritten(): return respective counters.
  - public LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts(): returns an unmodifiable defensive copy preserving insertion order. No method changes unrelated counters.

src/main/java/Cell.java:
- public final class Cell
  - private final String raw.
  - public static Cell of(String raw): if raw==null, store empty string; else store raw as-is.
  - public String raw(): returns stored raw.
  - public boolean isBlank(): returns raw.trim().isEmpty(). Immutable; no setters.

src/main/java/Row.java:
- public final class Row
  - private final List<String> header; private final List<Cell> cells; both copied defensively in constructor.
  - public Row(List<String> header, List<Cell> cells): copies inputs and may pad internal cells to header size using Cell.of("") if needed.
  - public List<String> header(): returns unmodifiable defensive copy or unmodifiable view that cannot be mutated by caller.
  - public List<Cell> cells(): returns unmodifiable defensive view of cells list.
  - public Cell get(String column): finds first index i in header with header.get(i).equals(column); if found and i < cells.size(), return cells.get(i); if not found or i>=cells.size(), return Cell.of("").
  - public LinkedHashMap<String,String> asStringMap(): builds an ordered map of header->cells[i].raw() for each header index; if cells shorter, empty string for missing.

src/main/java/Sorters.java:
- public final class Sorters
  - public static final class Order
    - private final String column; private final boolean ascending.
    - public Order(String column, boolean ascending)
    - public String column(): returns column.
    - public boolean ascending(): returns ascending.
  - public static Comparator<Row> comparator(List<Order> orders): returns a comparator that for each Order compares the corresponding Cell.raw() strings; blanks (cell.isBlank()) always sort after non-blanks regardless of ascending/descending; for non-blank comparisons use String.compareTo; apply ascending flag by reversing sign if needed; if tie across all orders, deterministically tie-break by comparing full Row as concatenated raw strings (e.g., iterate header order) to avoid nondeterminism; never use Java streams.

src/main/java/Sheet.java:
- public final class Sheet
  - private final String name; private final List<String> header; private final List<Row> rows.
  - public Sheet(String name, List<String> header, List<Row> rows): copies inputs defensively.
  - public String name(): returns name.
  - public List<String> header(): unmodifiable defensive header view.
  - public List<Row> rows(): unmodifiable defensive rows view.
  - public Sheet filter(Predicate<Row> predicate, ProcessingReport report): builds a new Sheet with only rows where predicate.test(row) is true; for each retained row, call report.incrementRowsKept() exactly once; does not change report.rowsRead or rowsWritten; header/name preserved.
  - public Sheet sort(List<Sorters.Order> orders): returns a new Sheet with rows sorted by Sorters.comparator(orders); no counter changes.

src/main/java/Workbook.java:
- public final class Workbook
  - private final LinkedHashMap<String, Sheet> sheets = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  - public Workbook()
  - public void addSheet(Sheet sheet): inserts/overwrites by sheet.name().
  - public Optional<Sheet> getSheet(String name): returns Optional.of(sheet) if present, else Optional.empty().
  - public Set<String> sheetNames(): returns unmodifiable defensive set copy preserving insertion order if applicable.

src/main/java/ValueParser.java:
- public final class ValueParser
  - public static Double toDouble(String raw, String column, ProcessingReport report): if raw==null or raw.trim().isEmpty(), return null without recording; else attempt Double.valueOf(trimmed); on NumberFormatException, call report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once and return null.

src/main/java/Filters.java:
- public final class Filters
  - public static Predicate<Row> equals(String column, String value): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().equals(value).
  - public static Predicate<Row> contains(String column, String fragment): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().contains(fragment).
  - public static Predicate<Row> numericGreaterThan(String column, double threshold, ProcessingReport report): for a given row, call ValueParser.toDouble once with row.get(column).raw(); if null return false; else return parsed > threshold.

src/main/java/Aggregations.java:
- public final class Aggregations
  - public static int count(Sheet sheet): returns sheet.rows().size().
  - public static double sum(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate rows once, call ValueParser.toDouble once per row; accumulate non-null values; ignore blanks/invalids; return 0.0 if none.
  - public static double average(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): as sum but divide by count of numeric values; return 0.0 if no numeric values.
  - public static Double min(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track smallest non-null; return null if none.
  - public static Double max(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track largest non-null; return null if none.
  - All methods must not use Java streams; use for loops and ArrayList.

src/main/java/CsvIO.java:
- public final class CsvIO
  - public static Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report): split by '\n' retaining order; first line is header split by ',' with negative limit to preserve trailing empties; for each subsequent line (data row), split with negative limit; pad to header length with empty strings; ignore excess cells; construct Cell for each field; wrap in Row; increment report.incrementRowsRead() exactly once per data row; return new Sheet(name, header, dataRows).
  - public static String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report): build string with header line (comma-joined) followed by each row as comma-joined cell.raw(); for every data row written, call report.incrementRowsWritten() exactly once; must not modify rowsRead or rowsKept; use '\n' line separators; do not quote commas or escape.

src/main/java/Main.java:
- public final class Main
  - public static void main(String[] args): prepare a fixed in-memory CSV string; use fresh ProcessingReport for each phase (import, filter, aggregation, export); invoke CsvIO.importCsvFromString, Sheet.filter, Sheet.sort, Aggregations.sum, CsvIO.toCsvString; print one concise deterministic summary; no input, no filesystem/network, no randomness, no threads, no streams.

Project-specific Java 11 in-memory spreadsheet processing contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java, src/main/java/Cell.java, src/main/java/Row.java, src/main/java/Sorters.java, src/main/java/Sheet.java, src/main/java/Workbook.java, src/main/java/ValueParser.java, src/main/java/Filters.java, src/main/java/Aggregations.java, src/main/java/CsvIO.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; all project classes are in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Surefire plugin. Java streams are forbidden throughout this small repository, especially `Stream.toList()` which does not exist in Java 11; use ordinary bounded loops and `java.util.ArrayList`
- ProcessingReport starts rowsRead, rowsKept, and rowsWritten at zero and owns a LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts. incrementRowsRead/incrementRowsKept/incrementRowsWritten add exactly one; recordInvalid(column) adds exactly one for that key; getters return counters; invalidCounts returns an unmodifiable defensive LinkedHashMap copy. No method changes an unrelated counter
- Cell is immutable: Cell.of(String raw) maps null to the empty string and otherwise preserves the string; raw() returns it and isBlank() tests raw.trim().isEmpty(). Row copies its header and cells, get(String column) returns the cell at the first equal header or Cell.of("") if absent, and header(), cells(), and asStringMap() return unmodifiable defensive values
- Sorters.Order(String column,boolean ascending) exposes column() and ascending(). Sorters.comparator(List<Order>) compares Cell.raw() strings in order, puts blank values last regardless of direction, and is deterministic. Sheet copies name/header/rows, exposes name(), header(), rows(), filter(Predicate<Row>,ProcessingReport), and sort(List<Sorters.Order>); filter increments rowsKept exactly once per retained row and neither operation changes rowsRead or rowsWritten
- Workbook is only an in-memory named-sheet container with addSheet, getSheet returning Optional, and sheetNames returning an unmodifiable defensive set
- ValueParser.toDouble(String raw,String column,ProcessingReport report) trims input, returns null without recording for null/blank, returns Double.valueOf for valid input, and on invalid input calls report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once then returns null. Filters.equals and contains perform string predicates; numericGreaterThan uses ValueParser once per tested row
- Aggregations exposes count, sum, average, min, and max. Each numeric method visits every row once and calls ValueParser.toDouble exactly once for that row; blank and invalid values are ignored, sum/average return 0.0 when no numeric value, min/max return null. Therefore one invocation of sum over one invalid `bad` cell records exactly one invalid count; tests must use a fresh ProcessingReport for each independent aggregation instead of expecting several aggregation calls to record one combined invalid event
- CsvIO has exactly two public static operations: `Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report)` and `String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report)`. The format is deliberately simple comma-separated text with no quoted commas. Import treats the first line as header, preserves empty fields by using split with a negative limit, pads short data rows, ignores excess cells, and calls incrementRowsRead exactly once per data row. Export emits the header and every data row with commas and newline separators, calls incrementRowsWritten exactly once per data row, and never changes rowsRead/rowsKept. There is no report-free export overload and no Reader/Writer/filesystem API

Bob,CA,1500

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java 11 in-memory spreadsheet processing contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java, src/main/java/Cell.java, src/main/java/Row.java, src/main/java/Sorters.java, src/main/java/Sheet.java, src/main/java/Workbook.java, src/main/java/ValueParser.java, src/main/java/Filters.java, src/main/java/Aggregations.java, src/main/java/CsvIO.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; all project classes are in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Surefire plugin. Java streams are forbidden throughout this small repository, especially `Stream.toList()` which does not exist in Java 11; use ordinary bounded loops and `java.util.ArrayList`
- ProcessingReport starts rowsRead, rowsKept, and rowsWritten at zero and owns a LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts. incrementRowsRead/incrementRowsKept/incrementRowsWritten add exactly one; recordInvalid(column) adds exactly one for that key; getters return counters; invalidCounts returns an unmodifiable defensive LinkedHashMap copy. No method changes an unrelated counter
- Cell is immutable: Cell.of(String raw) maps null to the empty string and otherwise preserves the string; raw() returns it and isBlank() tests raw.trim().isEmpty(). Row copies its header and cells, get(String column) returns the cell at the first equal header or Cell.of("") if absent, and header(), cells(), and asStringMap() return unmodifiable defensive values
- Sorters.Order(String column,boolean ascending) exposes column() and ascending(). Sorters.comparator(List<Order>) compares Cell.raw() strings in order, puts blank values last regardless of direction, and is deterministic. Sheet copies name/header/rows, exposes name(), header(), rows(), filter(Predicate<Row>,ProcessingReport), and sort(List<Sorters.Order>); filter increments rowsKept exactly once per retained row and neither operation changes rowsRead or rowsWritten
- Workbook is only an in-memory named-sheet container with addSheet, getSheet returning Optional, and sheetNames returning an unmodifiable defensive set
- ValueParser.toDouble(String raw,String column,ProcessingReport report) trims input, returns null without recording for null/blank, returns Double.valueOf for valid input, and on invalid input calls report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once then returns null. Filters.equals and contains perform string predicates; numericGreaterThan uses ValueParser once per tested row
- Aggregations exposes count, sum, average, min, and max. Each numeric method visits every row once and calls ValueParser.toDouble exactly once for that row; blank and invalid values are ignored, sum/average return 0.0 when no numeric value, min/max return null. Therefore one invocation of sum over one invalid `bad` cell records exactly one invalid count; tests must use a fresh ProcessingReport for each independent aggregation instead of expecting several aggregation calls to record one combined invalid event
- CsvIO has exactly two public static operations: `Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report)` and `String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report)`. The format is deliberately simple comma-separated text with no quoted commas. Import treats the first line as header, preserves empty fields by using split with a negative limit, pads short data rows, ignores excess cells, and calls incrementRowsRead exactly once per data row. Export emits the header and every data row with commas and newline separators, calls incrementRowsWritten exactly once per data row, and never changes rowsRead/rowsKept. There is no report-free export overload and no Reader/Writer/filesystem API
- Main.main uses one fixed in-memory CSV string, fresh reports for logically separate operations, prints at most one concise deterministic summary, and returns normally without input, network, filesystem, GUI, threads, clock, or randomness
- Because all project classes are in the unnamed/default package, MainTest imports only org.junit.jupiter.api.Test, static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions members, and ordinary java.util classes; it directly refers to project classes by simple name and must never emit invalid lines such as `import Sheet;`, `import CsvIO;`, or `import ProcessingReport;`
- MainTest contains exactly three concise tests and uses no streams: (1) runtime invokes `Main.main(new String[0])` and returns normally; (2) pipeline uses the literal CSV `Name,Country,Sales
Alice,US,1000
Bob,CA,1500
Charlie,US,2000`, imports with reportImport and asserts rowsRead==3, filters Country US with reportFilter and asserts rowsKept==2, then MUST literally assert `assertEquals("Alice", filteredRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Charlie", filteredRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`, sorts those two rows descending by Name and MUST literally assert `assertEquals("Charlie", sortedRows.get(0).get("Name").raw());` and `assertEquals("Alice", sortedRows.get(1).get("Name").raw());`, then sums Sales with a fresh reportAggregation and asserts 3000.0 and empty invalidCounts; Row itself has no raw() method, so `filteredRows.get(1).raw()` and every equivalent direct Row.raw() call are forbidden; (3) invalid/round-trip uses literal CSV `Name,Sales
Alice,1000
Bob,bad
Charlie,
Dana,2000`, calls sum exactly once with a fresh reportAggregation and asserts 3000.0 plus invalidCounts().get("Sales")==1, exports with a fresh reportExport and asserts rowsWritten==4, re-imports with a fresh reportReimport and asserts rowsRead==4, identical header, four rows, and Bob's Sales remains `bad`
- no test expects rowsKept immediately after import, no test expects rowsWritten after import or before calling the report-taking toCsvString, and no test reuses one ProcessingReport across sum/average/min/max while expecting only one invalid count
- repeat the exact file list, Java 11 no-stream rule, counter ownership, two-method CsvIO API, separate-report rule, default-package import ban, exact three fixtures, and exactly three test scopes in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Excel data processing.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java 11 in-memory spreadsheet processing contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: pom.xml, src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java, src/main/java/Cell.java, src/main/java/Row.java, src/main/java/Sorters.java, src/main/java/Sheet.java, src/main/java/Workbook.java, src/main/java/ValueParser.java, src/main/java/Filters.java, src/main/java/Aggregations.java, src/main/java/CsvIO.java, src/main/java/Main.java, src/test/java/MainTest.java; all project classes are in the default package
- pom.xml targets Java 11, declares JUnit Jupiter in test scope, and configures a JUnit-5-capable Surefire plugin. Java streams are forbidden throughout this small repository, especially `Stream.toList()` which does not exist in Java 11; use ordinary bounded loops and `java.util.ArrayList`
- ProcessingReport starts rowsRead, rowsKept, and rowsWritten at zero and owns a LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts. incrementRowsRead/incrementRowsKept/incrementRowsWritten add exactly one; recordInvalid(column) adds exactly one for that key; getters return counters; invalidCounts returns an unmodifiable defensive LinkedHashMap copy. No method changes an unrelated counter
- Cell is immutable: Cell.of(String raw) maps null to the empty string and otherwise preserves the string; raw() returns it and isBlank() tests raw.trim().isEmpty(). Row copies its header and cells, get(String column) returns the cell at the first equal header or Cell.of("") if absent, and header(), cells(), and asStringMap() return unmodifiable defensive values
- Sorters.Order(String column,boolean ascending) exposes column() and ascending(). Sorters.comparator(List<Order>) compares Cell.raw() strings in order, puts blank values last regardless of direction, and is deterministic. - public final class ProcessingReport

- ValueParser.toDouble(String raw,String column,ProcessingReport report) trims input, returns null without recording for null/blank, returns Double.valueOf for valid input, and on invalid input calls report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once then returns null. - Aggregations exposes count, sum, average, min, and max. Each numeric method visits every row once and calls ValueParser.toDouble exactly once for that row; blank and invalid values are ignored, sum/average return 0.0 when no numeric value, min/max return null. Therefore one invocation of sum over one invalid `bad` cell records exactly one invalid count; tests must use a fresh ProcessingReport for each independent aggregation instead of expecting several aggregation calls to record one combined invalid event

Export emits the header and every data row with commas and newline separators, calls incrementRowsWritten exactly once per data row, and never changes rowsRead/rowsKept. Bob,bad

  - public List<Cell> cells(): returns unmodifiable defensive view of cells list.

- public final class ValueParser

- public final class Filters

src/main/java/Aggregations.java:
- public final class Aggregations

- ProcessingReport starts rowsRead, rowsKept, and rowsWritten at zero and owns a LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts. incrementRowsRead/incrementRowsKept/incrementRowsWritten add exactly one; recordInvalid(column) adds exactly one for that key; getters return counters; invalidCounts returns an unmodifiable defensive LinkedHashMap copy. No method changes an unrelated counter
- Cell is immutable: Cell.of(String raw) maps null to the empty string and otherwise preserves the string; raw() returns it and isBlank() tests raw.trim().isEmpty(). src/main/java/ProcessingReport.java:
- public final class ProcessingReport
  - private int rowsRead, rowsKept, rowsWritten initialized to 0.
  - private LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts initialized empty.
  - public ProcessingReport()
  - public void incrementRowsRead(): increments rowsRead by exactly 1.
  - public void incrementRowsKept(): increments rowsKept by exactly 1.
  - public void incrementRowsWritten(): increments rowsWritten by exactly 1.
  - public void recordInvalid(String column): adds 1 to invalidCounts for key column exactly once per call; must not increment other counters.
  - public int getRowsRead(), getRowsKept(), getRowsWritten(): return respective counters.
  - public LinkedHashMap<String,Integer> invalidCounts(): returns an unmodifiable defensive copy preserving insertion order. No method changes unrelated counters.

src/main/java/Cell.java:
- public final class Cell
  - private final String raw.
  - public static Cell of(String raw): if raw==null, store empty string; else store raw as-is.
  - public String raw(): returns stored raw.
  - public boolean isBlank(): returns raw.trim().isEmpty(). Immutable; no setters.

src/main/java/Row.java:
- public final class Row
  - private final List<String> header; private final List<Cell> cells; both copied defensively in constructor.
  - public Row(List<String> header, List<Cell> cells): copies inputs and may pad internal cells to header size using Cell.of("") if needed.
  - public List<String> header(): returns unmodifiable defensive copy or unmodifiable view that cannot be mutated by caller.
  - public List<Cell> cells(): returns unmodifiable defensive view of cells list.
  - public Cell get(String column): finds first index i in header with header.get(i).equals(column); if found and i < cells.size(), return cells.get(i); if not found or i>=cells.size(), return Cell.of("").
  - public LinkedHashMap<String,String> asStringMap(): builds an ordered map of header->cells[i].raw() for each header index; if cells shorter, empty string for missing.

src/main/java/Sorters.java:
- public final class Sorters
  - public static final class Order
    - private final String column; private final boolean ascending.
    - public Order(String column, boolean ascending)
    - public String column(): returns column.
    - public boolean ascending(): returns ascending.
  - public static Comparator<Row> comparator(List<Order> orders): returns a comparator that for each Order compares the corresponding Cell.raw() strings; blanks (cell.isBlank()) always sort after non-blanks regardless of ascending/descending; for non-blank comparisons use String.compareTo; apply ascending flag by reversing sign if needed; if tie across all orders, deterministically tie-break by comparing full Row as concatenated raw strings (e.g., iterate header order) to avoid nondeterminism; never use Java streams.

src/main/java/Sheet.java:
- public final class Sheet
  - private final String name; private final List<String> header; private final List<Row> rows.
  - public Sheet(String name, List<String> header, List<Row> rows): copies inputs defensively.
  - public String name(): returns name.
  - public List<String> header(): unmodifiable defensive header view.
  - public List<Row> rows(): unmodifiable defensive rows view.
  - public Sheet filter(Predicate<Row> predicate, ProcessingReport report): builds a new Sheet with only rows where predicate.test(row) is true; for each retained row, call report.incrementRowsKept() exactly once; does not change report.rowsRead or rowsWritten; header/name preserved.
  - public Sheet sort(List<Sorters.Order> orders): returns a new Sheet with rows sorted by Sorters.comparator(orders); no counter changes.

src/main/java/Workbook.java:
- public final class Workbook
  - private final LinkedHashMap<String, Sheet> sheets = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  - public Workbook()
  - public void addSheet(Sheet sheet): inserts/overwrites by sheet.name().
  - public Optional<Sheet> getSheet(String name): returns Optional.of(sheet) if present, else Optional.empty().
  - public Set<String> sheetNames(): returns unmodifiable defensive set copy preserving insertion order if applicable.

src/main/java/ValueParser.java:
- public final class ValueParser
  - public static Double toDouble(String raw, String column, ProcessingReport report): if raw==null or raw.trim().isEmpty(), return null without recording; else attempt Double.valueOf(trimmed); on NumberFormatException, call report.recordInvalid(column) exactly once and return null.

src/main/java/Filters.java:
- public final class Filters
  - public static Predicate<Row> equals(String column, String value): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().equals(value).
  - public static Predicate<Row> contains(String column, String fragment): returns predicate evaluating row.get(column).raw().contains(fragment).
  - public static Predicate<Row> numericGreaterThan(String column, double threshold, ProcessingReport report): for a given row, call ValueParser.toDouble once with row.get(column).raw(); if null return false; else return parsed > threshold.

src/main/java/Aggregations.java:
- public final class Aggregations
  - public static int count(Sheet sheet): returns sheet.rows().size().
  - public static double sum(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate rows once, call ValueParser.toDouble once per row; accumulate non-null values; ignore blanks/invalids; return 0.0 if none.
  - public static double average(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): as sum but divide by count of numeric values; return 0.0 if no numeric values.
  - public static Double min(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track smallest non-null; return null if none.
  - public static Double max(Sheet sheet, String column, ProcessingReport report): iterate once, call ValueParser once per row; track largest non-null; return null if none.
  - All methods must not use Java streams; use for loops and ArrayList.

src/main/java/CsvIO.java:
- public final class CsvIO
  - public static Sheet importCsvFromString(String name, String csv, ProcessingReport report): split by '\n' retaining order; first line is header split by ',' with negative limit to preserve trailing empties; for each subsequent line (data row), split with negative limit; pad to header length with empty strings; ignore excess cells; construct Cell for each field; wrap in Row; increment report.incrementRowsRead() exactly once per data row; return new Sheet(name, header, dataRows).
  - public static String toCsvString(Sheet sheet, ProcessingReport report): build string with header line (comma-joined) followed by each row as comma-joined cell.raw(); for every data row written, call report.incrementRowsWritten() exactly once; must not modify rowsRead or rowsKept; use '\n' line separators; do not quote commas or escape.
